report.source_text: Given the immunocompromised status of the host, the Gram stain results triggered initiation of oral trimethoprim–sulfamethoxazole (TMP/SMX) to cover the possibility of infection with Nocardia species. When central nervous system (CNS) involvement was confirmed by neuroimaging, imipenem–cilastatin was added to the antibiotic regimen. At hospital discharge, imipenem–cilastatin was replaced with ceftriaxone based on microbial sensitivity, and oral TMP/SMX was continued. On development of nephrotoxicity 4 weeks after discharge, TMP/SMX was switched to linezolid. Intravenous ceftriaxone was continued for 12 weeks and then switched to oral minocycline for a planned 12-month course. However, minocycline was discontinued shortly thereafter due to gastrointestinal side effects. The patient was continued on linezolid monotherapy for 4 more months, bringing the total duration of antibiotic therapy to approximately 7 months.

clinician.final_diagnosis: infective endocarditis in the setting of disseminated nocardiosis
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 64-year-old heart transplant patient presented with fever, chills, a new holosystolic murmur, dullness to percussion and decreased breath sounds over the right lung base, and a tender right thigh. Initial workup included a transthoracic echocardiogram (TTE) showing moderate tricuspid regurgitation but no clear vegetation. Blood cultures eventually returned positive for Nocardia asteroides. Further imaging revealed disseminated infection: CT chest showed multiple peripheral lung nodules with a right-sided pleural effusion, and a transesophageal echocardiogram (TEE) revealed a small mobile mass on the tricuspid valve, confirming infective endocarditis. MRI of the right thigh demonstrated an abscess within the vastus lateralis muscle, indicating another site of dissemination. Treatment was initiated with oral trimethoprim–sulfamethoxazole (TMP/SMX), with imipenem–cilastatin added upon confirmation of CNS involvement by neuroimaging. The regimen was later adjusted to ceftriaxone and TMP/SMX, then linezolid due to nephrotoxicity, and ultimately linezolid monotherapy for a total of approximately 7 months.
